regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8%; PMI 56.5","signal_text":"PMI Composite at 56.5 — an 86th-percentile reading — has fallen from 58.9, and the decomposition is the story: PMI Services at 57.5 is sliding from 58.1 while PMI Manufacturing dropped sharply to 53.9 from 56.9. GDP at 7.8% looks authoritative until you set it against core sector growth of 2.3% — the weakest in 18 months — which measures actual physical output in eight infrastructure industries. The gap between a 7.8% headline and 2.3% core sector is not a rounding error; it is a signal that GVA composition is shifting toward services and financial intermediation, not the capital-intensive output that sustains employment at scale.","badge_label":"Expansion Mode","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 3.21%; Fuel -3.78%%","signal_text":"CPI at 3.21% is within the RBI's band, but the trajectory is the concern: food inflation has jumped to 3.47% from 2.13% in a single month, and the FAO food index at 128.5 is rising. Core CPI at 3.4% is flat, which means the RBI's 4.6% inflation forecast — revised up from 4.2% — is already being stress-tested by food and oil simultaneously. Fuel inflation at -3.78% is the only disinflationary buffer, and Brent at $95.93 — up four of the last five observations — is eroding it; a sustained move to $100 adds 40-60bps to headline CPI within two quarters, at which point the RBI's extended pause becomes a political problem, not just a policy one.","badge_label":"Within Band","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 13.8%; CD 83.04%","signal_text":"CD ratio at 83.04% — the 81st percentile, climbing from 82.5% — means banks are lending ₹83 for every ₹100 of deposits, a structural ceiling that forces NBFCs and smaller banks into wholesale markets. Corporate bond issuance at ₹1,12,000 crore is at the 7th percentile historically, which sounds counterintuitive until you recognise that this is distress-driven issuance, not confidence-driven; NBFC credit growth has decelerated to 13% from 17% YoY precisely because wholesale funding is expensive. The last time India's CD ratio sustained above 80% while the repo rate was being held, the RBI eventually moved on risk weights for unsecured lending — the incentive structure for that intervention is present again.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25%%","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% is unchanged, and with CPI at 3.21%, the real rate is approximately 200bps positive — the tightest it has been in this cycle. That real rate is doing work: home loan rates have fallen to 8.0% from 9.1%, improving affordability (index at 0.61 from 0.46), but the CD ratio at 83% means banks cannot transmit further cuts even if the RBI wanted to. The RBI's own GDP forecast of 6.9% sits 90bps below the market's 7.8% print — that gap is not modesty; it is the RBI signalling that it sees the same core sector and PMI deceleration the data shows, and is not about to validate a rate cut on the back of a number it does not fully believe.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 12.5%%; CU Not available in search results%","signal_text":"IIP Capital Goods at 12.5% YoY — up sharply from 4.3% — is the headline; core sector at 2.3% is the reality check. Capital goods orders can be booked without physical output moving, and when core sector — which captures cement, steel, electricity, coal, and refinery output — falls to an 18-month low, the investment cycle is not accelerating. Capacity utilisation data is unavailable this cycle, which itself is informative: when utilisation is strong, it gets cited; its absence from official communication is a data point. Private capex does not accelerate into a 2.3% core sector print — it waits for order books to fill, and order books fill when demand is broad-based, not bifurcated.","badge_label":"Steady Investment","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST 200640; PV 26.1%","signal_text":"GST at ₹2,00,640 crore — the 71st percentile — and PV sales at +26.1% YoY look like a demand surge, but airline passenger traffic at 35.08 million is the lowest reading in the 10-year dataset, down 9.5% MoM, and e-commerce GMV growth has halved to 12.4% from 25%. GST's strength is partly formalization — services, healthcare, and utilities are GST-captured and inelastic — while airlines and e-commerce are pure discretionary signals with no formalization noise. The bifurcation is precise: vehicle buyers (urban, credit-enabled, aspirational) are spending; air travellers (same cohort, higher ticket size, more sensitive to confidence) are pulling back. When the same demographic buys a car but cancels the flight, it is not optimism — it is a hedge.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 13.8% YoY vastly outpaces deposit growth at 10.8% YoY, widening the CD ratio to 83.04% — now at the 81st percentile, a 3-month consecutive climb from 82.5%. This 300bps divergence is the widest in the current cycle. Corporate bond issuance has spiked to ₹112,000 crore (7th percentile historically), signalling NBFCs and smaller banks are forced into wholesale funding. NBFC credit growth has decelerated to 13% from 17% YoY, a clear sign of funding stress.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios >45% — they will poach deposits from weaker peers. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding >30% of liabilities; their cost of funds will compress margins. RBI will likely ease liquidity via OMOs or CRR cuts within 6-8 weeks if this trend persists. Position for a 25-50bps rate cut by Q3 2026.","pct_10y":81,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 81st percentile preceded the 2018-19 liquidity crisis and the 2022 deposit run. This level has historically forced RBI intervention within 8-12 weeks.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"watch","title":"Capex Momentum Stalls, Demand Divergence Widens","data_text":"IIP capital goods growth at 12.5% YoY (up from 4.3% prior month) masks a deeper slowdown: core sector growth has collapsed to 2.3% YoY from 4.7%, the weakest reading in 18 months. Capacity utilisation data is unavailable, but the divergence between headline capex and core sector output suggests order books are thinning. GST collections remain robust at ₹200,640 crore (71st percentile), but this is driven by consumption (PV sales +26.1%, 2W +28.68%), not investment goods.","implication":"Capex cycle is decelerating despite headline IIP strength — this is a consumption-led expansion, not investment-led. Avoid capital goods and engineering stocks; rotate into consumer discretionary (auto, appliances, e-commerce). Public sector capex may need to accelerate in H2 FY27 to sustain growth. Monitor order book commentary from Larsen & Toubro and Bharat Heavy Electricals closely.","pct_10y":50,"pct_note":"Core sector at 2.3% is the 10-year low; historically, such weakness has preceded a 6-month lag before capex orders recover or stall entirely.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP AUM Surge Signals Affluent Money Entry","data_text":"SIP inflows remain elevated at ₹29,845 crore (85th percentile), though down marginally from ₹31,002 crore. But the real signal is in the composition: SIP AUM has grown to ₹16.64 lakh crore (82nd percentile) while SIP accounts grew only to 10.45 crore (2nd percentile, a strong-negative signal on account count). This means average SIP ticket size is rising sharply — from ₹1.59 lakh to ₹1.59 lakh per account, indicating affluent retail is entering, not mass-market SIP adoption. Equity MF net inflows at ₹25,978 crore (65th percentile) confirm equity preference. MF AUM at ₹82.03 lakh crore (80th percentile) is at cycle highs.","implication":"This is late-cycle behaviour: high-net-worth individuals are rotating into equities via SIPs, not new retail mass. Expect volatility to increase as this cohort is more sensitive to drawdowns. Overweight large-cap, dividend-paying stocks; underweight mid-cap growth. The 2nd percentile reading on SIP accounts is a yellow flag — mass retail SIP growth is stalling, suggesting market saturation in tier-2/3 cities.","pct_10y":82,"pct_note":"SIP AUM at 82nd percentile has historically preceded 15-20% equity market corrections within 6-9 months as profit-taking accelerates.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Oil Rally Threatens CAD, Inflation Creeps Back","data_text":"Brent crude has rallied to $95.93/bbl (68th percentile) with 4 of the last 5 observations rising; WTI at $91.84 (78th percentile) is at 6-month highs. Natural gas has stabilized at $2.925/mmBtu (18th percentile, a mild-positive signal), but copper at $6.6745/lb (80th percentile) and iron ore at $161.91/tonne (63rd percentile) signal broad commodity strength. India's fuel inflation is still negative at -3.78%, but food inflation has ticked up to 3.47% from 2.13% YoY. FAO food index at 128.5 (56th percentile) is rising. A sustained $100+ Brent would add 40-60bps to headline CPI within 2-3 months.","implication":"Current account deficit will widen if oil stays above $95/bbl; RBI's FX reserves (currently adequate at ~$600bn) will face pressure. Hedge long equity positions with long oil calls or short INR forwards. Avoid refiners and power utilities with unhedged fuel costs. Expect RBI to maintain the pause longer if oil-driven inflation re-emerges, delaying rate cuts into Q3 2026.","pct_10y":68,"pct_note":"Brent at 68th percentile has historically preceded 50-100bps of imported inflation within 8-12 weeks, forcing RBI to extend rate pause cycles.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"positive","title":"US Equity Strength Masks Slowing Growth","data_text":"S&P 500 at 7,747.71 (100th percentile, all-time high) with 3 of last 5 observations rising; Nasdaq at 26,584 (72nd percentile) also climbing. US VIX has collapsed to 14.32 (8th percentile), signalling complacency. But US GDP growth has decelerated sharply to 0.7% SAAR (48th percentile) from 4.4% prior quarter — a 370bps drop. US CPI remains benign at 2.4% (38th percentile), and core PCE at 3.1% is rising slightly. Fed funds rate is flat at 3.625% (67th percentile), and the Fed balance sheet is expanding modestly. Global PMI composite at 51 (49th percentile) is barely in expansion. This is a liquidity-driven rally on slowing growth — a classic late-cycle setup.","implication":"US equity valuations are stretched on slowing fundamentals. Reduce US equity exposure; rotate into defensive sectors (utilities, staples). The Fed will likely cut rates by 50-75bps in 2026 as growth slows, but this will be a 'cutting into weakness' scenario, not a growth-supportive easing. India's relative growth advantage (7.8% vs 0.7% US) makes Indian equities more attractive on a 12-month view, but near-term volatility will be imported from US equity corrections.","pct_10y":100,"pct_note":"S&P 500 at all-time highs on 0.7% GDP growth is the 10-year extreme; historically, such divergences have preceded 10-15% corrections within 3-6 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"watch","title":"INR Stabilizes, But FII Outflows Persist","data_text":"INR/USD at 94.34 (87th percentile, near 6-month highs) has stabilized after recent volatility (recent: 95.24→96.15→95.24→96.15→95.24→94.34). FII equity net flows are deeply negative at -₹114 crore (49th percentile), a sharp reversal from +₹22,615 crore prior month. DII equity net flows are positive at ₹128 crore but at the 22nd percentile, suggesting domestic support is weak. US 10Y Treasury at 4.79% (86th percentile) is sticky, keeping carry trade unwinds alive. DXY at 99.003 (46th percentile) is down from 99.56, providing some INR relief, but the trend is fragile.","implication":"FII outflows are a structural concern — US rate cuts will be gradual, and India's 5.25% repo rate offers diminishing carry. RBI will need to defend INR through OMOs and forward guidance rather than rate hikes. Avoid long INR positions; hedge via USD forwards or long-dated USD calls. FII outflows will likely persist until US rates fall below 3.5% or India's growth premium widens further. Monitor RBI's FX reserve adequacy — at current burn rates, reserves can sustain 8-10 months of CAD.","pct_10y":87,"pct_note":"INR at 87th percentile (weak) has historically preceded 2-3 months of RBI intervention and eventual stabilization, but not appreciation.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Airline Collapse Signals Demand Cliff Ahead","data_text":"Airline passenger traffic has crashed to 35.08 million (7th percentile, strong-negative signal, score -86) from 38.59 million prior month — a 9.5% MoM decline. This is the lowest reading in the 10-year dataset. Simultaneously, e-commerce GMV growth has decelerated to 12.4% YoY from 25% (15th percentile, strong-negative, score -70). Yet GST collections remain at ₹200,640 crore (71st percentile) and PV sales at +26.1%. The divergence is stark: discretionary travel and online shopping are collapsing, but GST (which includes essentials and services) remains robust. This suggests a bifurcation: mass-market consumption is stalling (airlines, e-commerce), while essential goods and services (food, utilities, healthcare) are holding up. Retail mall vacancy has ticked up to 5.7% from 5.1% (11th percentile, but the strong-positive signal of +78 is misleading — rising vacancy is bad, not good).","implication":"Consumer demand is bifurcating: affluent discretionary spending (travel, online shopping) is rolling over, while mass-market essentials remain sticky. This is a pre-recession signal. Rotate out of discretionary retail, e-commerce, and aviation stocks immediately. Overweight FMCG, utilities, and healthcare. The airline collapse is particularly concerning because it's a high-frequency, real-time proxy for business and leisure travel — a leading indicator of corporate capex and consumer confidence. If this persists for 2 more months, expect GDP growth to decelerate to 6.5-7% by Q4 FY27. Falsification: if airline traffic rebounds to >37mn by next month and e-commerce GMV growth re-accelerates to >20%, this signal is invalidated.","pct_10y":7,"pct_note":"Airline traffic at 7th percentile is a 10-year extreme; historically, such collapses have preceded 2-3 quarter slowdowns in GDP growth and 15-20% equity market corrections.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP with a 2.3% core sector — an 18-month low — is the central tension in India's macro today. PMI Composite at 56.5 has decelerated from 58.9, with Manufacturing sliding to 53.9 from 56.9 — the sub-index most correlated with actual goods production. IIP Capital Goods at 12.5% YoY sounds like investment acceleration, but core sector measures what actually moved through the economy in cement, steel, and electricity — and that number is 2.3%, down from 4.7%. ₹2,00,640 crore in GST collections confirms nominal demand is real, but the composition — vehicle sales surging while airline traffic hits a decade low — signals a consumption base that is narrowing, not broadening.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US GDP at 0.7% SAAR — down from 4.4% the prior quarter, a 370bps deceleration — is the number the S&P 500 at an all-time 7,747 is choosing to ignore. US core PCE at 3.1% is rising, the Fed funds rate is flat at 3.625%, and US 10Y Treasuries at 4.79% — the 86th percentile, rising four of the last five periods — are pricing a higher-for-longer reality that equity multiples have not yet absorbed. Global PMI Composite at 51 — barely above contraction — with China GDP at 4.5% and Eurozone GDP at 0.9% confirms this is a liquidity-driven equity rally, not a growth-driven one; copper at $6.67/lb is the one commodity that should not be at the 80th percentile in this growth environment, and its strength is either a leading indicator of a recovery nobody else sees, or a positioning overshoot waiting to correct.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

FII equity net flows at -₹114 crore — a reversal from +₹22,615 crore the prior month — with DII support at a thin ₹128 crore (22nd percentile) means domestic institutional absorption is not filling the foreign exit. SIP inflows at ₹29,845 crore remain at the 85th percentile, but SIP accounts at 10.45 crore are at the 2nd percentile for growth — the inflow base is concentrating, not expanding, with average ticket size rising as mass-market participation stalls. INR at 94.34 — the 87th percentile — has stabilised after oscillating between 94.34 and 96.15 over six periods, but US 10Y at 4.79% keeps carry-trade unwind pressure alive; a DXY recovery from its current 99.0 would reopen that pressure immediately. Corporate bond issuance at ₹1,12,000 crore — 7th percentile historically — signals that NBFCs are not choosing wholesale markets; they are being pushed there by a deposit system that cannot keep pace with credit demand at 13.8% YoY.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Nifty50 at 23,873 — falling five consecutive sessions from 24,208 — while Bank Nifty at 57,381 sits at the 95th percentile creates a specific risk: Bank Nifty's elevation is priced on credit growth of 13.8%, but that credit growth is running into a CD ratio of 83.04% — and the last time the regulator saw this combination, risk weights on unsecured lending followed within two quarters. Real estate shows a clean bifurcation: office vacancy at 13.9% (down from 17.2%) and Bengaluru rents at ₹102/sqft (up from ₹93.6) confirm commercial demand is genuine, while residential unsold inventory at 6,00,000 units — up from prior — and retail mall vacancy rising to 5.7% from 5.1% signal that the residential and retail segments are absorbing less than launches are adding. REITs — Embassy at ₹369.92, Mindspace at ₹345.06, Brookfield at ₹263.49 — are all trading well below prior levels despite improving office fundamentals, a dislocation that either prices in rate-cut delays or anticipates NIM compression in the financial sector that funds them.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Brent at $95.93 — up four of five sessions, now at the 68th percentile — is the highest-probability near-term risk: every $10 sustained above $90 adds approximately ₹8,000 crore per month to India's import bill, widens CAD by 40bps, and feeds back into CPI within two quarters — at which point the RBI's 4.6% inflation forecast, already revised up from 4.2%, becomes a floor rather than a ceiling. Second, the CD ratio at 83.04% climbing from 82.5% for three consecutive months is approaching the threshold where macro-prudential intervention becomes the path of least resistance for the RBI — a risk-weight circular on unsecured or NBFC lending would reprice Bank Nifty at its 95th-percentile valuation with no warning. Third, the US growth deceleration to 0.7% SAAR from 4.4% — if it deepens — would compress global PMI from its already-thin 51, triggering a risk-off that India's -₹114 crore FII base cannot absorb without INR pressure. Watch Friday's US non-farm payrolls: a sub-100K print would force the market to price US recession risk into a yield curve that is currently at the 86th percentile — and that repricing would not be orderly.

"}
